title: Ashish Nehra Calls Gill and Pandya "North Pole and South Pole" as Captains
excerpt: The Gujarat Titans head coach compared his two skippers' contrasting leadership styles, backing the reserved Shubman Gill to grow into India's captaincy while praising Hardik Pandya's openness and trust.
body:
• Gujarat Titans head coach Ashish Nehra described Shubman Gill and Hardik Pandya as "north pole and south pole" in their captaincy approaches, speaking at a Cricket Association of Bengal awards ceremony.
  • Nehra said Pandya completely trusted him and was open to conversations, while Gill is more reserved and observant but equally keen to learn.
  • Gill led GT to the 2026 IPL final after Pandya had guided the franchise to the title in 2022 and another final in 2023.
  • Nehra also commented on Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli, saying it is too early to rule them out of the 2027 ODI World Cup.

Two Very Different Leaders

Gujarat Titans head coach Ashish Nehra has offered a candid comparison of the two men who have captained the franchise since its inception, describing Shubman Gill and Hardik Pandya as polar opposites in their leadership DNA.

https://x.com/CNNnews18/status/2097022571724300475

Speaking as a special guest at the Cricket Association of Bengal awards ceremony on Monday, the former India left-arm pacer drew a vivid distinction between the skipper who won the franchise its title and the one now steering it forward.

"They are very, very different. You are talking about north pole and south pole. Both of them were not somebody who has done much captaincy, but you learn on your way forward, and suddenly somebody is pretty much doing captaincy for India in two formats."

— Ashish Nehra, Gujarat Titans head coach

Pandya: The Open Communicator

Nehra painted Pandya as a captain who led through constant dialogue. Under Pandya and Nehra's partnership, Gujarat Titans won the IPL title in their debut season in 2022 and reached the final again in 2023 before the all-rounder returned to his boyhood franchise Mumbai Indians.

"One thing is for sure — he completely trusted me, which was the perfect, perfect thing," Nehra said. "He will always be keen to learn. He will always ask if something doesn't go right or doesn't go well. He is somebody you can have lots of conversations with."

Gill: The Quiet Observer

Gill, who took over the captaincy after Pandya's departure, has brought a different temperament to the role. The 26-year-old led Gujarat Titans to the 2026 IPL final, where they lost to Royal Challengers Bengaluru, while also captaining India in ODIs and T20Is.

"Shubman is a little reserved, a little shy, but that's okay. Everyone is different. There is no right or wrong," Nehra said. "He is someone who will not talk or have as many conversations as Hardik Pandya, but he is to the point. He is somebody who is very keen to learn and keen to observe."

Nehra was emphatic that Gill's quieter style should not be mistaken for a lack of growth. "Of course, he is a work in progress. He is only 26-27, and it is not that he has been doing captaincy for so many years. It is only one or two seasons, and you learn things and you will get better."

On Rohit and Kohli's World Cup Future

Nehra also weighed in on the futures of Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli, both of whom have stepped back from shorter formats. Asked whether the two veterans would feature in the 2027 ODI World Cup, the GT coach was cautious.

"It is too early to say if Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli will play the 2027 World Cup," Nehra said, leaving the door open for India's most decorated active batters to return to 50-over cricket if they choose to.

What It Means for Indian Cricket Fans Abroad

The Gill-versus-Pandya comparison matters well beyond franchise cricket. Gill is now India's captain in two white-ball formats and a key figure in the Test side, making his leadership trajectory a subject of global interest among diaspora fans who follow every India tour and IPL season closely.

Nehra's endorsement of Gill as a captain still evolving — but evolving in the right direction — adds nuance to a conversation that too often reduces captaincy to win-loss records. For a generation of Indian cricket fans, how Gill grows in the role may define the next era of the sport.
